transcript: Down an unsuspecting street in the East Village, through a doorway in an animal mural. This is Baku, which means punishment in Japanese. So I turn to some more, which is a new app in the city I'm kind of obsessed with, which has a ton of recommendations of cool experiences to do in New York with videos and real reviews. Anyway, actually used to be a English teacher in Asia, and I thought this would be a really fun experience for us to do together, and it totally was. Botsu is Japanese game show. It's an improv game show with a ton of different games. All of them have random rules, and then the loser of each round get a box you for a punishment. Like taking a body shot off of a freezer, getting shot with a ball, putting your hands on a tray of mousetrap, or even just having to be beat up by a wrestler. Feels chaotic because it is, but it was so much fun to watch. Also, they give you a headband if you're wearing it. This is the famous Batsu chicken, and they played this egg laying game with people from the audience. Don't worry, you had to find a waver. There's no force participation. Foxy has been in New York for 13 years and I have no idea how I did not know. They also have shows in Chicago and London. It would be a perfect night out with friends or for a birthday. Party! They had good drinks and affordable food. And truly, I cannot remember the last time I laughed this hard. What a silly, goofy, fun ooze mix.
